To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the post-growth fabrication of chirped Bragg gratings is demonstrated in III-V material for the first time, (2) a 5-nm wide stopband with 1.7 ps/nm dispersion was demonstrated, (3) a DFB laser based on a chirped grating was fabricated and characterized.
the chirped grating is fabricated using a tapered geometry and the resulting device has a 5-nm wide stopband and 0.033 ps/nm dispersion.

(1) the post-growth integrated CBG in GaAs–Al0.3Ga0.7As is fabricated by a simple etching and polishing process and (2) the CBG is used to demonstrate a DFB laser with a 5-nm tuning range and a 0.033 ps/nm dispersion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, characterization and applications of integrated chirped Brag grating (CBGs) devices.
the fabrication of integrated Bragg reflectors on GaAs/AlGaAs material using a post-growth etching process.
the fabrication of a chirped grating on a III-V semiconductor material using a post-growth process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of chirped Bragg gratings in semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOAs) is a promising technique for improving the performance of these devices.
the post-growth fabrication of a chirped Bragg gratings on GaAs-AlGaAs is a viable approach to the realization of high-performance integrated optical devices.
a chirp-free laser is a good laser and a chirp-prone laser is a bad laser.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chirp of the Bragg grating is a key parameter for the design of DFB lasers and that the fabrication of a chirped grating with a desired chirp is a key challenge.
the fabrication and characterization of post-growth integrated Bragg gratings in III-V semiconductors is now well established.
the post-growth fabrication and characterization of chirped Bragg gratings (CBGs) on GaAs/AlGaAs waveguides is demonstrated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fabrication and characterization of post-growth integrated CBGs on GaAs– AlGaAs are possible.
the postgrowth fabrication of CBG structures in III–V material is feasible, and that the taper method provides an elegant and flexible method for the implementation of arbitrary chirp functions.
the tapered CBG can be implemented in a variety of material systems with different refractive index contrast and can be used for a wide range of applications.
